primitives.name: Predictive Metamodel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using 29 college football rating systems, data for 5925 games during 2016–24, and a _k_-fold cross-validation process focused on model predictiveness, a five-system metamodel is developed to predict the victory margin for games in the ensuing week.
primitives.assumptions: The model assumes that linear combinations of existing rating systems can capture predictive power beyond individual models.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when new rule changes introduce unprecedented variables not covered by the 29 base models.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Predictive posterior distribution of game outcomes given covariates. GSE: State-transition kernel for game evolution based on metamodel predictions.
layer2.telemetry: Out-of-sample prediction accuracy on holdout weeks

primitives.name: _k_-fold Cross-Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using 29 college football rating systems, data for 5925 games during 2016–24, and a _k_-fold cross-validation process focused on model predictiveness, a five-system metamodel is developed to predict the victory margin for games in the ensuing week.
primitives.assumptions: Data points are independent and identically distributed, and the cross-validation error estimates generalization error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when temporal autocorrelation violates i.i.d. assumption.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Holdout set validation for posterior predictive checks. GSE: Training/validation splits for policy evaluation in sequential decision processes.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validated mean squared error on holdout sets

primitives.name: Betting Line Adjustment
primitives.verbatim_quote: The model achieves strong results vis-à-vis the opening, midweek, and closing betting lines, and is statistically significant in the presence of the opening line in validation and test samples.
primitives.assumptions: The betting line is an unbiased estimate of true probability, and the adjustment captures residual systematic bias.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during sharp market movements or information asymmetry.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Posterior mean adjusted for bookmaker bias as optimal prediction. GSE: State-action value function conditioned on market signals.
layer2.telemetry: Residual standard deviation after accounting for betting line

primitives.name: Benchmark Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The model is potentially useful for the College Football Playoff committee, media, fans, the betting market, and oddsmakers, and provides a benchmark against which future rating systems can be assessed.
primitives.assumptions: The metamodel represents a reasonable baseline performance achievable by any new system.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where new systems must outperform the ensemble to justify development effort.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Prior distribution for evaluating new predictive models. GSE: Performance ceiling for reinforcement learning policies.
layer2.telemetry: Average rank among competing rating systems

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is combining heterogeneous predictive signals (rating systems) into a coherent forecast. The metamodel treats each base model as a noisy measurement of true team strength. By optimizing linear coefficients via cross-validation, the approach mitigates overfitting while leveraging diverse algorithmic perspectives. Key failure modes include distribution shift (e.g., rule changes) and multicollinearity among highly correlated inputs. The statistical significance test ensures the added value is not spurious noise.
